extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents and practitioners filing/prosecuting applications at the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, timelines, and work-sharing/acceleration programme rules for prosecuting patent applications at IPOS (including responses to written opinion, requests for review, PPH/GPPH, ASPEC, translations, third-party observations, and re-registration with Cambodia/Laos).

rubrics_metrics.name: No response to Written Opinion — automatic establishment and Notice of Intention to Refuse
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not respond to the written opinion, the system will automatically establish the 'Examination Report without response to Written Opinion' and 'ER cover sheet (no response to WO) bypass Examiner' cover page with the latest written opinion. A Notice of Intention to Refuse will also be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an automatic procedural outcome when no response is filed to the written opinion; triggers the pathway towards refusal unless the applicant acts (see request for examination review or file required forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of request prior to report issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant intends to withdraw the request and switch to other routes, he may write in via eCommunications before the examination report and Notice of Eligibility/Notice of Intention to Refuse are issued. The Formalities officer will notify the applicant on the withdrawal outcome. Any amendments filed in response to written opinion will still be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must notify before issuance; withdrawal outcome communicated by Formalities officer. Amendments already filed may still be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of retraction of Written Opinion by Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Patent Examiner retracts a written Opinion/invitation to amend that has been issued to the applicant, any Patents Form 13A filed in response to this written opinion will be considered as void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction nullifies responses filed in reliance on that written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on withdrawal of Patents Form 13A
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where there is a change of mind regarding the set of amendments filed, the withdrawal of Patents Form 13A will not be allowed. Applicants may, if the forms can still be filed within the allowable time period, file another set of amendments to replace the former approved Patents Form 13A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once PF13A is filed/approved withdrawal is not permitted; replacement amendments only if still within deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Eligibility and requirement to file Patents Form 14
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examination/supplementary examination report contains no objections or unresolved issues, a Notice of Eligibility will be issued to the applicant with the report. The applicant may proceed to request for grant of patent by filing Patents Form 14 within 2 months from the date of the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file Patents Form 14 within 2 months will lead to automatic abandonment (system action, entry in register and Patents Journal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Intention to Refuse — request for examination review (Patents Form 12B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examination/supplementary examination report contains unresolved objections, a Notice of Intention to Refuse will be issued to the applicant with the report. The applicant may proceed to request for examination review report by filing Patents Form 12B within 2 months from the date of the notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Patents Form 12B is not filed within the timeline, the system will automatically refuse the patent application at the end of 2 months from the Notice of Intention to Refuse; status updated and refusal published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Examination Review Report — allowed contents and how to file
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may submit written submissions in response to the Patent Examiner’s opinion (mandatory) and/or amendments to specification (optional) with Patents Form 12B. From 30 Oct 2017, instead of filing Patents Form 13 separately, applicants who wish to make amendments to the specification when requesting for an examination review report may submit the proposed amendments along with Patents Form 12B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written submission is mandatory with Form 12B; amendments may be included with Form 12B per the stated dates and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment document format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1 Apr 2017, both marked-up amendments and clean copies of the amended sheets are required. From 1 Dec 2019, if amendments have been made to claims, a marked-up and clean copy of the full set of claims have to be submitted together with the request. The amendments or corrections should be reflected similarly in both the clean and marked-up copies. The request for amendments to specification should set out the reasons for making amendments and any evidence in support thereof should also be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter 5.1.12 for accepted format of marked-up copies. Reasons and evidence must accompany amendment requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer checklist for accepting a Form 12B request
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the request is received, the Formalities officer will review requirements: a) application must be lodged on or after 14 Feb 2014; b) Notice of Intention to Refuse was issued; c) the form is filed within the timelines (or extension via Patents Form 45 approved); d) written submission is submitted; e) any amendments submitted with both marked-up and clean copies; f) representation details and/or address for service correspond with record (or Form CM1/CM2 filed); g) if applicant indicates prior disclosure within 12 months prior to filing, criteria and documents in Chapters 6.1.18–6.1.24 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any requirements are not met the Formalities officer will issue a letter inviting clarification or rectification within 2 months; reminders issued if not rectified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for correction of errors and updating representation
rubrics_metrics.description: To rectify errors, the applicant may file Form CM4 and indicate the relevant rule (Rules 58 and/or 91). Types include 'Correction of Form lodged', 'Correction of Specification of a Patent or of an Application for a Patent', and 'Correction of any other document relating to a Patent or an Application for a Patent'. To update representation details (not a correction of error), file Form CM1 or CM2. To submit clarification letters or documents in response to the Registrar's letter, reply via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow forms and rules referenced; use eCommunications for replies. Failure to rectify leads to reminders and potential refusal of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Review Report outcomes and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination review report need not specify whether the Patent Examiner agrees or disagrees with the examination report, search and examination report or supplementary examination report, if amendments to the specification are submitted with the request for examination review report to overcome all unresolved objections. If the examination review report contains no objections or unresolved issues, a Notice of Eligibility will be issued; if there are unresolved issues, a Notice of Refusal of the patent application will be issued with the negative examination review report (refusal takes effect at the end of 2 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes feed the usual paths: eligibility -> file PF14 within 2 months or abandonment; unresolved issues -> refusal after 2 months, entry and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to communicate with Registry or Patent Examiner about reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant would like to raise issue(s) with the report, he may write in via eCommunications. If the error identified is valid, a corrected report will be issued to the applicant with revised timelines, if applicable. The report containing the error will be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifications on Examiner’s comments can be sought via eCommunications; arrangements for direct communication reference Chapter 11.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examiner‑initiated informal communication practice
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOS launched Patent Examiner-initiated informal communications (email, phone, face-to-face interviews) to improve prosecution efficiency. Such communications will be initiated via an email containing the purpose of the communication and proposed actions to be taken by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal comms may invite filing of PF13A, CM4 or an invitation to amend. Amendments filed with PF13A after an informal communication should be made within the time period for filing a response to written opinion or invitation to amend. Applicant should only file necessary amendments related to specified claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples where Examiner may initiate informal communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: a) where subject matter relates to an emerging technology and the Examiner finds the applicant’s explanation would benefit prosecution; b) when application is ready for grant except for minor clarity issues in pending claims; c) when no substantive progress after several iterations and an interview may help close prosecution gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal communications are aimed at efficiency and may lead to invitations to amend or interviews to expedite resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official record of informal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the mode of communication, all communications regarding the merits of an application form part of the official file records. For phone or a face-to-face interview, an interview minute would be created and placed on file record to ensure transparency. The file record will be made available for inspection via Form CM10 (but not available on Patents Open Dossier until further notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect formal recordkeeping of informal interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations timing and form
rubrics_metrics.description: For a published application undergoing Search and Examination, observations by third party can be made in writing to the Registrar on the question whether the invention is a patentable invention, stating reasons for the observations before the issuance of the examination report, search and examination report or supplementary examination report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations must be submitted as an eCommunication using document type 'Third Party Observations'. Supporting documents are strongly encouraged. There is no official form and no fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations supporting documents and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registrar may direct the third party to furnish supporting documents and file an English translation of the whole or relevant parts if the documents are not in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations and additional documents may be requested; ensure accessibility and translation where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of late third‑party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations received after the establishment of the examination report, search and examination report or supplementary examination report will be put on record but will not be forwarded to the Patent Examiner, nor will it be made available on the Patents Open Dossier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is critical — to be effective observations must be received before establishment of the relevant report.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH purpose and reliance on earlier work products
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) is a work-sharing programme where the examination of a patent application in one IP Office can be accelerated by referencing the examination results from another IP Office. The examination results relied upon are the patent search and examination results (national work products) of the partnering IP Office; for EPO and PCT-authorities, PCT work products may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH/GPPH accelerates prosecution at no additional official cost and may be requested at filing of Form 11/12 or later (if examination has not begun).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of PPH requests accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Types: a) Mottainai (PPH request is made in the Office of Later Examination); b) PCT-PPH (based on PCT work products from an ISA or IPEA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different linking rules (same earliest date or priority) apply depending on type and bilateral arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to make a PPH request (timing and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH/GPPH may be requested at the point of filing the request for search and examination, or examination report by indicating 'ASPEC/PPH' on Patents Form 11 or 12 and submitting relevant documents. PPH request can still be made after Form 11/12 is filed if examination has not begun by writing in via eCommunications with subject 'PPH acceleration requested' citing corresponding application number and whether amendments are required to conform claims. If amendments required, Examiner will issue invitation to amend and applicant should respond via Patents Form 13A selecting PPH and filing PF13A with amendments and relevant PPH documents within 2 months from invitation to amend. If no amendments required, IPOS will invite submission of PPH documents via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified eCommunications subject and include necessary details; adhere to invitations and two-month filing windows where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH request formal requirements (IPOS Formalities review checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formalities officer will review: a) PPH is selected on PF11/PF12 form; b) IPOS application and application forming basis of PPH request are corresponding applications or related sharing the same earliest date (for CNIPA/SAIP special filing-order rules apply); c) all office actions of the relied-upon application are submitted; d) list of allowable/patentable claims submitted, with at least one claim determined allowable/patentable by the other IP Office; e) for GPPH, if documents are available in other office’s Dossier Access System they need not be submitted (English translation submitted if not in English; VET not required); f) all claims in IPOS application must sufficiently correspond to one or more claims found allowable/patentable by the other IP Office and a claims correspondence table is submitted; g) cited documents referred to in the results may be submitted (not mandatory unless requested) and English translations may be requested if not in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document completeness and claims correspondence are key to PPH acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple related applications for PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may rely on the search and examination results of more than one related application (OFF/OEE) for PPH/GPPH. All relevant documents and multiple sets of claim correspondence tables are required to be furnished accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple earlier examinations are used, provide clear mapping and all supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility of utility model/petty patent allowed claims for PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowed claims from a utility model or a petty patent cannot be used to form the basis for requesting PPH in IPOS as they are not required to meet the same patentability criteria as a standard patent, and typically are not subject to substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only results from substantively examined standard patents are acceptable bases for PPH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation rules for documents relied upon in PPH/GPPH
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an English translation of the documents is required, machine-translation is acceptable. If the Patent Examiner finds the machine translation is of poor quality and difficult to understand, the applicant may be required to submit a manual translation. The manual translation does not have to be certified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machine translations permitted but be prepared to supply manual (non-certified) translations if quality is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC purpose and non‑binding nature of partner findings
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC is a regional patent work-sharing programme among participating ASEAN Member States IP Offices. Participating AMS IP Offices may refer to and consider search and examination results received under ASPEC but are not obliged to adopt findings; each office proceeds according to its national laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC is intended to reduce work and improve search/examination but does not override domestic law or final decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC request eligibility — corresponding/related national phase linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application in a participating AMS IP Office where the ASPEC Request Form is filed ('second IP Office') is required to be a pending corresponding/related national phase entry patent application in the other participating AMS IP Office ('first IP Office'). Corresponding/related means linked by Paris Convention priority claim, or both having same priority claim from another member, or both being national phase entries from the same PCT application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the two applications satisfy one of the linkage definitions before relying on ASPEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC request procedures and document requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC request may be submitted at any time before the final decision of grant or refusal via the e-ASPEC platform. When received, Formalities officer will review: a) ASPEC option selected or written notice submitted; b) Search and Examination result or Written Opinion of corresponding application submitted; c) list of claims referred to in the results submitted, with at least one claim determined allowable/patentable; d) all claims in IPOS application must sufficiently correspond to one or more claims found allowable/patentable by the first IP Office; e) English translation of documents submitted if not in English, with translation verified by a translator or by the patent agent before IPOS, if requested; f) optional supporting documents may include claim correspondence table, list of prior art with English translations, cited documents, and written opinion with translations if not relying on written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification of translations may be required; provide claim mapping and supporting prior art where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT‑ASPEC procedure and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT-ASPEC extends ASPEC to include use of PCT results (written opinions of ISA/IPEA, IPER). Applicant should indicate PCT-ASPEC on cover letter or ASPEC form and email the monitoring authority with PCT application number, desired 2nd AMS and application number, date of request, and applicant’s name. PCT-ASPEC is a pilot capped at 100 eligible requests per year (27 Aug 2019 – 26 Aug 2025 extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the email notification steps and be mindful of the annual cap for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC AIM — Industry 4.0 prioritisation and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC AIM prioritises Industry 4.0 patent applications; AMS will issue first actions within 6 months. Applicant should indicate ASPEC AIM on cover letter or request form and email monitoring authority with details (application no., desired second IP Office etc.). ASPEC AIM pilot capped at 50 eligible requests per year (27 Aug 2019 – 26 Aug 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check IPOS website for listed IPC codes relating to Industry 4.0 and apply early given the cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent cooperation re-registration with Cambodia and Laos — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under cooperation, Singapore patents may be re-registered in Cambodia or Laos or IPOS-issued report submitted for grant in those offices, subject to priority linkage. Conditions for re-registration: Cambodia — (a) Singapore patent must be in force at time of lodgement; (b) filing date on or after 22 Jan 2003; (c) must meet Cambodian patentability (e.g., not pharmaceutical). Laos — (a) Singapore patent must be in force at lodgement; (b) filing date on or after 17 Jan 2002; (c) must meet Laotian patentability requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure force and filing date thresholds and substantive patentability compliance with Cambodian/Laotian laws before relying on re-registration route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness rules for response filings (forms and consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple provisions require filing within stated timelines (e.g., PF14 within 2 months of Notice of Eligibility; PF12B within 2 months of Notice of Intention to Refuse; PF13A responses within response-to-WO timelines). Failure to meet timelines results in automatic system actions such as abandonment or refusal and publication/entry in register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict adherence to the specified time limits is mandatory; where applicable seek extension via Patents Form 45 before deadlines.
